subject: Materials Science
title: Metal Matrix Composites
description: A 60-second lesson on Metal Matrix Composites.

hook.text: Aluminum is light but soft. Add silicon carbide particles and it becomes armor-hard.

buildup.text: Metal matrix composites embed ceramic particles or fibers inside a metal — usually aluminum.

discovery.text: The ceramic reinforcement boosts stiffness, wear resistance, and high-temperature strength.

twist.text: MMCs are tough to machine — the hard particles eat through cutting tools quickly.

climax.text: Brake rotors on high-performance cars use aluminum–SiC composites for lighter, cooler stops.

punchline.text: Sprinkle ceramic into metal and it stops wearing out.

quiz.question: What is a challenge of metal matrix composites?
options: They are too soft for structural use
Hard reinforcement particles make machining difficult
They corrode faster than pure metals
